markets.name: Brazil
humour: Zoeira: playful self-irony, 'we laugh so we don't cry'
Memes built on soap operas, catchphrases and nursery rhymes
Self-deprecating jokes about everyday frustrations, with resilient optimism
markets.verdict: Biggest opportunity: a huge audience, among the least nervous about AI, and meme-mad.
markets.ai_view: Among the least nervous of the 32 countries surveyed; Latin America leans positive on AI.

markets.name: Spain
humour: Affiliative humour about everyday situations wins on TikTok
Absurd and surreal humour travels well
markets.verdict: Strong second language: a big TikTok audience and mid-range pay. Respect the classics.
markets.ai_view: Slightly more nervous than the 50% average; Europe leans cautious.

markets.name: Indonesia
humour: Satire set in fictional worlds rather than real ones
watch: Halal always: no pork or alcohol, not even in jokes
Religion, ethnicity and race (SARA) are off-limits
markets.verdict: Most AI-positive region and a huge audience, but pays little. Keep humour wholesome-silly, not gross.
markets.ai_view: Asia leads the world in AI optimism; 91% want AI use disclosed, the highest surveyed.

markets.name: Portugal
humour: Memes: everyday life (70%), fails and mistakes (56%), absurd (50%)
Brazilian humour is the favourite foreign humour
watch: 42% have been offended by a tasteless joke: keep it warm, not nasty
markets.verdict: Small but loves humour. Reach it through the Brazilian account first, then test its own.

ideas.title: Receita da vó
ideas.idea: Comfort classics done properly (feijoada, pão de queijo, coxinha), framed as grandma's recipe.
ideas.why: Nostalgia and family classics are safe, shareable and evergreen.

ideas.title: Nordeste week
ideas.idea: A week of Northeastern dishes: acarajé, tapioca, baião de dois, cuscuz.
ideas.why: Northeastern street food and regional pride are trending themes on Brazilian TikTok.

ideas.title: Brigadeiro lab
ideas.idea: Dessert-slot series of brigadeiro twists: pistachio, churros, ninho, bicho de pé.
ideas.why: A national favourite that fits the two-desserts-a-week rhythm.

ideas.title: Festa Junina table
ideas.idea: Pamonha, canjica, paçoca, pé de moleque and corn cake for the June festivals.
ideas.why: The biggest food festival of the year outside Christmas.

ideas.title: Christmas in summer
ideas.idea: Rabanada, salpicão, chocotone desserts and cold dishes for a 35°C Christmas.
ideas.why: A twist Northern-hemisphere content never covers.

ideas.title: Geladeira vazia
ideas.idea: 'Empty fridge' budget dinners from whatever is left.
ideas.why: Everyday frustrations like food prices are a top meme theme; cheap recipes meet them with optimism.

ideas.title: Dishes named after everyday pains
ideas.idea: Fake dishes like 'Torta do boleto atrasado' (overdue-bill pie) or 'Pudim de segunda-feira' (Monday pudding).
ideas.why: Zoeira is self-irony about shared hardships, with resilient optimism.

ideas.title: Novela-drama recipe
ideas.idea: A cursed dish told like a soap-opera cliffhanger, with dramatic captions or voiceover.
ideas.why: Brazilian memes lean heavily on soap operas and catchphrases.

ideas.title: Cursed national icons
ideas.idea: Affectionate NOT FOOD versions of coxinha, feijoada or açaí bowls.
ideas.why: Brazilians mock what they love; pride and embarrassment mix in their humour.

ideas.title: Sound-led Reels, evening posting
ideas.idea: Add trending Brazilian sounds in the app (funk, forró, sertanejo) and post 19:00-22:00 on weekdays.
ideas.why: Music drives Brazilian TikTok trends; activity peaks in the evening.

ideas.title: Stay out of politics
ideas.idea: No politicians, parties or election jokes; football banter only lightly.
ideas.why: Political memes are huge in Brazil but deeply polarised.

ideas.title: Con o sin cebolla
ideas.idea: Perfect tortilla de patatas, with the caption asking: team onion or no onion?
ideas.why: Everyday-situation humour and friendly debates drive comments on Spanish TikTok.

ideas.title: Supermarket-shelf recipes
ideas.idea: Recipes built around viral, seasonal and limited-edition supermarket products, plus high-protein and ready-meal upgrades.
ideas.why: Seasonal, limited-edition and viral products drove 2025's record food engagement; TikTok alone had 160M+ interactions.

ideas.title: Classics by the rules
ideas.idea: Paella valenciana, fabada, salmorejo made strictly traditionally, with the rules on the slides.
ideas.why: Spanish food purists punish shortcuts: the 2016 chorizo-paella backlash.
ideas.note: Get a classic wrong and it gets roasted; have it checked.

ideas.title: Roscón de Reyes
ideas.idea: Three Kings ring cake, with the hidden figurine and bean.
ideas.why: The big sweet of the Christmas season in Spain.

ideas.title: Torrijas for Semana Santa
ideas.idea: Spain's Holy Week French toast, plus variations.
ideas.why: The signature Easter sweet.

ideas.title: Cold soups season
ideas.idea: Gazpacho, salmorejo and ajoblanco through the heat.
ideas.why: Seasonal staples from June to August.

ideas.title: Family-dinner chaos
ideas.idea: 'La tortilla de la suegra', the mother-in-law's tortilla made of kitchen sponges, and other family-meal disasters.
ideas.why: Affiliative humour about shared everyday situations performs best.

ideas.title: Cursed paella (NOT FOOD)
ideas.idea: A deliberately everything-in 'paella' labelled NOT FOOD, asking people to rate the crime.
ideas.why: Turns purist outrage into the joke, on purpose.

ideas.title: Menú del día from another dimension
ideas.idea: A chalkboard set menu of surreal dishes, revealed course by course.
ideas.why: Absurd humour plus a format every Spaniard knows.

ideas.title: Twelve grapes, but wrong
ideas.idea: The New Year's Eve twelve grapes replaced with absurd props.
ideas.why: A ritual everyone does at midnight on 31 December.

ideas.title: No regional politics or bullfighting
ideas.idea: Keep Catalan, Basque and independence topics, and bullfighting, out entirely.
ideas.why: Divisive topics that split audiences.

ideas.title: Takjil for buka puasa
ideas.idea: Sweet snacks for breaking the fast: kolak, es buah, gorengan, bubur sumsum.
ideas.why: Ramadan is the biggest food-content season of the year.

ideas.title: Kue Lebaran
ideas.idea: Eid cookies: nastar, kastengel, putri salju.
ideas.why: Every family bakes or buys them for Lebaran.

ideas.title: Nusantara week
ideas.idea: Regional dishes from across the archipelago, with local ingredients.
ideas.why: Indonesia has about 27,000 local foods; TikTok and the Ministry of Health are pushing local-food content (2026).

ideas.title: Indomie upgrades
ideas.idea: Instant-noodle hacks for students and boarding-house cooks (anak kos).
ideas.why: Cheap, fast and universal.
ideas.note: Editorial judgement; not from a cited study.

ideas.title: Sambal levels
ideas.idea: One base sambal, five heat levels, from mild to 'call the fire brigade'.
ideas.why: Spice tolerance is a natural challenge format.

ideas.title: Receh pun captions
ideas.idea: Dad-joke puns about each dish in the caption and on the last slide.
ideas.why: 'Humor receh' and jokes bapak-bapak are among the most shared formats.

ideas.title: Cute-weird, not gross
ideas.idea: Absurd but wholesome fake dishes (a cloud-stuffed martabak, a karaoke bakso) instead of bodily gross-out.
ideas.why: Silly, gentle humour fits better than shock.
ideas.note: Test before committing to gross content here.

ideas.title: 17 Agustus lomba dishes
ideas.idea: Silly dishes inspired by Independence Day village games, like the cracker-eating race.
ideas.why: Everyone knows the games; they are playful by nature.

ideas.title: Halal, always
ideas.idea: No pork, lard or alcohol (including mirin, wine, rum), even in NOT FOOD jokes.
ideas.why: A Muslim-majority audience; getting this wrong is not a joke.

ideas.title: No religion or SARA
ideas.idea: Keep religion, ethnicity, race and inter-group topics out entirely.
ideas.why: A comedian was reported to police over religious jokes in January 2026; TV comics are advised to avoid SARA.

ideas.title: Label AI clearly
ideas.idea: Say the recipes and photos are AI-made in the bio and every caption.
ideas.why: 91% of Indonesians want AI use disclosed, the highest of 32 countries.

ideas.title: Bacalhau, one of 365 ways
ideas.idea: A running series of salt-cod dishes: à Brás, com natas, à Gomes de Sá.
ideas.why: The saying goes there's a bacalhau recipe for every day of the year.

ideas.title: Pastel de nata at home
ideas.idea: Custard tarts and variations for the dessert slots.
ideas.why: The national sweet, loved worldwide too.

ideas.title: Santos Populares sardines
ideas.idea: Grilled sardines on bread, caldo verde and festival food.
ideas.why: Lisbon and Porto's June street festivals.

ideas.title: São Martinho chestnuts
ideas.idea: Roast chestnuts and autumn dishes.
ideas.why: The St Martin's Day tradition.

ideas.title: Consoada
ideas.idea: Christmas Eve bacalhau with greens, then rabanadas and bolo-rei.
ideas.why: The main Christmas meal is on the 24th.

ideas.title: Receita que correu mal
ideas.idea: Kitchen-fail stories: the recipe that went wrong, as a NOT FOOD post.
ideas.why: Mistakes and failures are the second most popular meme type (56%).

ideas.title: Sunday lunch at avó's
ideas.idea: Everyday family-meal situations: the overfeeding grandmother, the leftovers that never end.
ideas.why: Everyday-life memes are the most popular (70%); family is where 78% laugh most.

ideas.title: Absurd pastelaria
ideas.idea: Surreal fake pastries in a bakery window.
ideas.why: Half of meme fans (50%) pick absurd humour.

ideas.title: Portugal vs Brazil banter
ideas.idea: Friendly food rivalry: whose pastel, whose bacalhau.
ideas.why: A long-running playful rivalry, including the 2016 'meme war'.

ideas.title: Reach Portugal via Brazil first
ideas.idea: Run Brazilian Portuguese first; launch a European Portuguese account only if Portuguese followers show up.
ideas.why: Brazilian humour is Portugal's favourite foreign humour; Porto prefers Brazilian content.

ideas.title: Warm, not nasty
ideas.idea: Avoid aggressive or tasteless jokes; laugh with people, not at them.
ideas.why: 42% have been offended by a tasteless joke.

ideas.title: Write natively, never translate
ideas.idea: Claude writes each market's recipes and jokes in the language, with local ingredients, units and references.
ideas.why: Many memes only make sense locally and don't translate.

ideas.title: Disclose AI everywhere
ideas.idea: Keep the AI note in bios and captions in every language.
ideas.why: 80% across 32 countries want AI use disclosed.
